chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Mufrid al-Hajj (one performing exclusive Hajj): does he bring forward his Tawaf or delay it? He said, 'He brings it forward.' A man next to him said, 'But my Sheikh did not do that; when he arrived, he stayed in Fakh until the people returned to Mina, then he went with them.' I said to him, 'Who is your Sheikh?' He said, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both).' I asked about the man, and he was the half-brother of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) from the mother's side.

key_terms.مُفْرِدِ الْحَجِّ: Mufrid al-Hajj (one performing exclusive Hajj without Umrah)

ai.seo_question: When should a Mufrid al-Hajj perform their Tawaf, upon arrival or after returning from Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the juristic flexibility in Hajj rituals, specifically contrasting Imam al-Sadiq’s permissive ruling for Mufrid pilgrims to perform Tawaf immediately upon arrival with the established practice of Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), who delayed it until returning from Mina. The narration underscores the scholarly tradition of respecting diverse, valid practices (ikhtilaf) within the Ahl al-Bayt, demonstrating that neither approach is erroneous but rather reflects different levels of caution or convenience. This context is vital for understanding how Shia fiqh accommodates varying methods of worship while maintaining ritual validity.
